Living Well / Free resources

Reading, listening & participation

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Find support for the format and activity you actually need, from a readable article to a more accessible conversation.

Access is a useful outcome in its own right. Reading view, spoken text, live transcription, visual descriptions, and a full screen reader address different barriers. Start with the person and task, not an assumption that a summary is always the answer.

Start with: Chrome: reading mode. Try one font or spacing adjustment before changing several settings at once.

Explore display and spoken-reading options before replacing a page with a summary.

Spoken reading · Free to browse

iPhone: hear selected text

Apple

A built-in route to hearing text or typing feedback when that is a better way to encounter the material.

Begin here: Choose the matching iOS guide and try a short non-sensitive passage.

Access: Free instructions; requires a compatible iPhone. Device, voice, and network requirements vary by feature.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open iPhone: hear selected text

Context & source

Keep private text from being spoken where others can hear it. Read-aloud support is not a claim of perfect comprehension or a replacement for accessible originals.

Speech-to-text support · Free to browse

Live Transcribe: conversation access

Google

Consider live text as one way to make a willing conversation easier to follow.

Begin here: Read the microphone, language, and history instructions; agree on use with the other person.

Access: Free public instructions. The feature needs a supported Android device and permissions; offline language support depends on the device.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Live Transcribe: conversation access

Context & source

Recognition can miss words, names, and negation. Confirm consequential details directly and review history settings before using it around private conversations.

Android Reading mode

Screen reader · Free core app

NVDA: a Windows screen reader

NV Access

A dedicated access tool for using supported computer interfaces through speech or braille.

Begin here: Begin with NV Access documentation and learning material appropriate to your needs.

Access: Free open-source Windows screen reader. Compatible hardware is needed; optional support and training products may cost money.

Perspective: Accessibility software from its nonprofit developer; not a clinical recommendation.

Open NVDA: a Windows screen reader

Context & source

A screen reader and a simple read-aloud button serve different needs. Suitability is individual, and authors remain responsible for accessible content.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Ask the person what helps, preserve working support, and verify important meaning against the original. These are source-reviewed options, not individual assessments or a promise that every feature works with every device.
